rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When asked what glorifying God means, the Prophet defined it as declaring Him free of every defect.
rows.anchor: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن فقال تنزيه الله عن كل سوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word tasbih is linked to swimming: a swimmer moves through water without sinking or becoming contaminated, as a bird moves through air.
rows.anchor: وأصله من سبح فإن السابح يسبح في الماء كالطير في الهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled form conveys distancing God from what cannot be ascribed to Him, covering His essence, attributes, and acts in affirmation and negation.
rows.anchor: والتشديد للتبعيد لأنك تسبحه أي تبعده عما لا يجوز عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wholly unreceptive to what is improper, just as a fish does not accept impurity; this explains tasbih as transcendence in essence, attributes, and acts.
rows.anchor: لأن السمكة كما أنها لا تقبل النجاسة فكذا الحق سبحانه لا يقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes tasbih to mean prayer, since the Qur’an uses the term that way.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن المراد بالتسبيح الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the command with the eight units of gratitude prayer the Prophet performed on the day of the conquest.
rows.anchor: عني به صلاة الشكر صلاها يوم الفتح ثمان ركعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others identify it as the forenoon prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : هي صلاة الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view divides eight units into four for gratitude and four for the forenoon prayer.
rows.anchor: صلي ثمان ركعات أربعة للشكر وأربعة الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is called tasbih because it necessarily contains glorification; this also calls for purifying prayer’s words and actions from defects.
rows.anchor: وتسمية الصلاة بالتسبيح لما أنها لا تنفك عنه وفيه تنبيه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: After the surah came down, the Prophet often said a formula glorifying God, praising Him, and seeking forgiveness and repentance.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد نزول هذه السورة يكثر أن يقول

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: The Prophet frequently said in bowing, Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You; forgive me.
rows.anchor: كان الرسول يقول كثيرا في ركوعه سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك اللهم اغفر لي

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In his final period, the Prophet repeatedly said the formula in every posture and explained that he had been commanded to do so.
rows.anchor: كان نبي الله في آخر أمره لا يقوم ولا يقعد ولا يذهب ولا يجيء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: After the surah was revealed, the Prophet often glorified God, sought forgiveness, and called Him the Oft-Returning and Forgiving.
rows.anchor: لما نزلت هذه السورة كان عليه السلام يكثر أن يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet also said that he sought God’s forgiveness one hundred times each day.
rows.anchor: إني لأستغفر الله كل يوم مائة مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih and praise suffice as thanks for victory and conquest, and the Qur’an gives prayer special honor alongside fasting.
rows.anchor: الآية تدلى على فضل التسبيح والتحميد حيث جعل كافيا في أداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is far superior to fasting because mosques belong to God and prayer contains remembrance, which is greater.
rows.anchor: فهذا يدل على أن الصلاة أفضل من الصوم بكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer’s form depends on revelation, while praise of God is known as worthy by reason and religious teaching; prayer is therefore adorned with glorification and magnification.
rows.anchor: أما كيفية الصلاة فلا سبيل إليها إلا بالشرع ولذلك جعلت الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says that if tasbih is not obligatory, it ranks below other prayer acts; Razi replies that other acts need obligation, whereas hearts naturally love glorification.
rows.anchor: سائر أفعال الصلاة مما لا يميل القلب إليه فاحتيج فيها إلى الإيجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command form normally implies obligation; even those who read it as recommendation should take it as obligatory here because it is joined to obligatory seeking of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: والأمر المطلق للوجوب عند الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further answer says tasbih was left nonobligatory because punishing its omission would itself make its special honor too conspicuous.
rows.anchor: لو وجبت لكان العقاب الحاصل بتركها أعظم إظهارا لمزيد تعظيمها

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: One reading says to combine the words Glory be to God and praise be to God in amazement at His remarkable favors, like mixing water with milk.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف أي قل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praising God already includes glorifying Him, since praise and gratitude entail declaring Him free of defects; this explains the Qur’an’s opening with praise and the Prophet’s praise at the conquest.
rows.anchor: إذا حمدت الله فقد سبحته لأن التسبيح داخل في الحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition can mark circumstance: glorify God while praising Him, as one might say to go out armed.
rows.anchor: سبح حامدا كقولك : اخرج بسلاحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean to glorify God intending to praise Him afterward, joining the two acts in intention when they cannot be joined verbally.
rows.anchor: أن يكون معناه سبح مقدرا أن تحمد بعد التسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition may mean by God’s favor and guidance rather than by anyone else’s; Aisha’s reply in the slander episode illustrates the phrasing.
rows.anchor: فعلت هذا بفضل الله ، أي سبحه بحمد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aisha said, by God’s praise, not yours, and the Prophet reportedly said, praise be to God for praise itself.
rows.anchor: حديث الإفك قول عائشة : ( بحمد الله لا بحمدك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The phrase may mean glorify by the command of your Lord.
rows.anchor: سادسها : روى السدي بحمد ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the preposition is treated as extra, the command can mean to choose the purest and finest praises for God.
rows.anchor: اختر له أطهر المحامد وأزكاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading urges cleansing praise of ostentation, reputation-seeking, and corrupt worldly aims.
rows.anchor: طهر محامد ربك عن الرياء والسمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise must not claim to have rendered God the honor due to Him, since people have not rightly measured Him.
rows.anchor: طهر محامد ربك عن أن تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih can stand in for the praise owed for blessings, since God’s favors are beyond human enumeration and thanks.
rows.anchor: فأت بالتسبيح والتنزيه بدلا عن الحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih and praise should arrive together: neither can be delayed behind the other, so the servant becomes both praiser and glorifier at once.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز تأخير أحدهما عن الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command can refer to purifying the heart by contemplating the Lord’s praise: seeing all things as from God removes attention to one’s own effort.
rows.anchor: أي طهر قلبك بواسطة مطالعة حمد ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih negates everything besides God, while praise recognizes that all things come from God.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى نفي ما سوى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation links the command to forgiving the people entering Islam: requesting forgiveness for the sinless signals that the Prophet should pardon them and abandon revenge.
rows.anchor: الاستغفار لمن لا ذنب له لا يحسن فعلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذا الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending with al-Tawwab presents acceptance of repentance as God’s characteristic practice, whether the repentant person is an enemy or ally and from Mecca or Medina.
rows.anchor: إن قبول التوبة حرفته فكل من طلب منه التوبة أعطاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the conquest, when the Meccans called him a generous brother and cousin, the Prophet declared there would be no reproach and cited Joseph’s forgiveness; he said God had commanded him to seek forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the command concerns the Prophet’s own forgiveness, one view allows that repeated seeking forgiveness makes his sin minor.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع أن تكون كثرة الاستغفار منه تؤثر في جعل ذنبه صغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view says he had to seek forgiveness so it would repair a minor sin without diminishing his reward.
rows.anchor: لزمه الاستغفار ليصير الاستغفار جابرا للذنب الصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny that he sinned say that seeking forgiveness functions like tasbih, since it describes God as the Forgiving.
rows.anchor: أن استغفار النبي جار مجرى التسبيح وذلك لأنه وصف الله بأنه غفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness is worship and an example for others, since even an infallible Prophet working diligently cannot dispense with it.
rows.anchor: تعبده الله بذلك ليقتدي به غيره إذ لا يأمن كل مكلف عن تقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the Prophet’s seeking forgiveness to concern leaving the better course.
rows.anchor: أن الاستغفار كان عن ترك الأفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every act of obedience falls short when measured against God’s beneficence, so the servant seeks forgiveness for that shortfall.
rows.anchor: فإذا قابلها بإحسان الرب وجدها قاصرة عن الوفاء بأداء شكر تلك النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual traveler seeks forgiveness after moving beyond each station because the prior station then appears inadequate; the stations and this forgiveness have no limit.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت مراتب السير إلى الله غير متناهية لا جرم كانت مراتب هذا الاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may instead concern forgiveness for the community, which God also commands in another verse; the whole community makes that request still more important.
rows.anchor: أمره بالاستغفار لذنب أمته في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi asks why the verse orders tasbih, then praise, then forgiveness, although repentance should precede obedience and praise should precede glorification.
rows.anchor: التوبة مقدمة على جميع الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer is that the order descends from the noblest to the less noble, since descent from Creator to creation is nobler than ascent from creation to Creator.
rows.anchor: فالأشرف نازلا إلى الأخس فالأخس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer says the servant’s tasbih and praise look sinful beside God’s majesty, so they call for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: إذا صار مقابلا بجلال الله وعزته صار عين الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih and praise honor God’s command like prayer, while seeking forgiveness shows compassion for creation like almsgiving; prayer precedes almsgiving.
rows.anchor: كما أن الصلاة مقدمة على الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet had to proclaim tasbih and forgiveness aloud so the whole community could transmit the surah reliably and know he delivered revelation fully.
rows.anchor: حتى يبقى نقل القرآن متواترا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s public act also made him a model for the community to renew thanks when blessings arrive, in ease and hardship.
rows.anchor: أن يصير الرسول قدوة للأمة حتى يفعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike ordinary people who tend to praise at the outset, the Prophet was told to praise and seek forgiveness at every time; at the announcement of his approaching death this also modeled what the community should do near death.
rows.anchor: فأمر الله رسوله بالحمد والاستغفار دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi asks why the verse says God was al-Tawwab in the past when people need acceptance in the future; he begins an answer by recalling the community’s honor and God’s prior acceptance of lesser peoples’ repentance.
rows.anchor: ألست أثنيت عليكم بأنكم : { خير أمة أخرجت للناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also asks why the verse uses al-Tawwab rather than al-Ghaffar, and why it says Lord and al-Tawwab rather than Allah; those answers continue in the next segment.
rows.anchor: قال : غفارا كما قاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers the question about past tense by citing the maxim that God acted well in the past and will do so in what remains.
rows.anchor: لقد أحسن الله فيما مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls the servant His namesake, first as a believer and then, through repentance, as al-Tawwab, while the shared names have different meanings.
rows.anchor: كنت لي سميا من أول الأمر أنت مؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God accepts repentance repeatedly, the servant too should repent often.
rows.anchor: يقبل التوبة كثيرا فنبه على أنه يجب على العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person can ask forgiveness with the tongue while persisting in sin, which is like mocking God.
rows.anchor: المستغفر بلسانه المصر بقلبه كالمستهزىء بربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The maxim that God did well in the past and will do well in what remains supports confidence in His future acceptance.
rows.anchor: لقد أحسن الله فيما مضى كذلك يحسن فيما بقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike al-Ghaffar, al-Tawwab can describe a servant who repents; God invites the servant to become His namesake by repenting often, while God accepts repentance repeatedly.
rows.anchor: لا يقال في صفات العبد غفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tawwab distinguishes sincere repentance from merely asking forgiveness while persisting in sin; endings of deeds should be repentance, and the Prophet reportedly ended every sitting with forgiveness.
rows.anchor: لم يجلس مجلسا إلا ختمه بالاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God balances the names Lord and al-Tawwab: nurturing comes first and accepting repentance comes last.
rows.anchor: فذكر اسم الذات مرتين وذكر اسم الفعل مرتين

rows.speaker: العباس
rows.claim: The Companions agreed the surah announced the Prophet’s death; Abbas understood this and wept, and the Prophet confirmed it.
rows.anchor: روى أن العباس عرف ذلك وبكى فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explained the surah as announcing the Prophet’s death; the Prophet praised his knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولكن نعيت إليه نفسه

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: In the report about Umar’s council, Ibn Abbas’ interpretation is that the surah announced the Prophet’s death, and the Prophet praised his knowledge.
rows.anchor: لقد أوتي هذا الغلام علما كثيرا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: After the surah was revealed, the Prophet said God had given a servant a choice between this world and meeting Him in the afterlife, and the servant chose the meeting.
rows.anchor: إن عبدا خيره الله بين الدنيا وبين لقائه والآخرة فاختار لقاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of the death reading is that the Prophet preached after the surah and mentioned that divine choice.
rows.anchor: إنما عرفوا ذلك لما روينا أن الرسول خطب عقيب السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completion of victory, conquest, and mass conversion signals that the Prophet’s mission had reached fullness, which is followed by decline and death.
rows.anchor: إذا تم شيء دنا نقصه توقع زوالا إذا قيل تم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted command to glorify, praise, and seek forgiveness would occupy the Prophet rather than the community; it signals that the mission of conveying revelation was complete.
rows.anchor: اشتغاله به يمنعه عن الاشتغال بأمر الأمة فكان هذا كالتنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness hints that the appointed time is near and that a wise person should prepare by increasing repentance.
rows.anchor: تنبيه على قرب الأجل كأنه يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet attained his worldly aim in victory and conquest and could now move to the better afterlife promised to him.
rows.anchor: فلما وجدت أقصى مرادك في الدنيا فانتقل إلى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the stronger view is that the surah came before the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: الأصح هو أن السورة نزلت قبل فتح مكة

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Those dating it after the conquest report that the Prophet lived sixty days after its revelation, continually glorifying God and seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ذكر الماوردي أنه عليه السلام لم يلبث بعد نزول هذه السورة إلا ستين يوما

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil gives a different chronology: the Prophet lived a year after the surah, then successive periods after verses on perfected religion, inheritance, the messenger from among the people, and return to God.
rows.anchor: عاش بعدها حولا ونزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi leaves the conflicting reports about the Prophet’s final days to God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: والله أعلم كيف كان ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation purpose is worship; al-Kafirun contrasts the Prophet’s obedience and rejection of partners with the unbelievers’ worship of idols, while al-Nasr promises worldly victory and afterlife reward and al-Masad threatens worldly loss and afterlife punishment.
rows.anchor: ثم بين في سورة : { قل ياأهل * أيها * الكافرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between servants’ outcomes raises why God permits this disparity; the answer is that He tests people with what He grants, swiftly punishing rebels and forgiving and rewarding the obedient.
rows.anchor: ليبلوكم * فيما * ءاتاكم } فكأنه قيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When commanded to warn his nearest kin, the Prophet called the Quraysh clans at al-Safa and said he could offer no worldly or afterlife share unless they affirmed God’s unity; Abu Lahab objected, and the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله يكتم أمره في أول المبعث ويصلي في شعاب مكة ثلاث سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In another occasion report, the Prophet called the Quraysh to verify his warning before announcing a severe punishment; Abu Lahab protested and the surah came down.
rows.anchor: صعد الصفا ذات يوم وقال : يا صباحاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third report says the Prophet fed his uncles from a small dish that miraculously fed them all, then invited them to Islam; Abu Lahab objected that Muslims would be equal, and condemned the religion.
rows.anchor: جمع أعمامه وقدم إليهم طعاما في صحفة فاستحقروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth report says Abu Lahab deterred visitors by calling the Prophet mad; when one delegation insisted on meeting him, Abu Lahab insulted him, the Prophet grieved, and the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: كان إذا وفد على النبي وفد سألوا عمه عنه

none: section heading and verse heading only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes tabbat to mean destruction; an old woman’s nickname and the verse about Pharaoh’s plot illustrate ruin.
rows.anchor: التباب الهلاك ، ومنه قولهم شابة أم تابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Bedouin who had intercourse while fasting said he was ruined and had ruined his fast; since the Prophet did not deny him, Razi infers that abandoning a part of faith brings ruin, especially with Abu Lahab’s disbelief, speech, and actions.
rows.anchor: لما واقع أهله في نهار رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation reads tabbat as loss that leads to destruction, as in the verse saying Pharaoh’s followers only increased him in loss.
rows.anchor: والتياب هو الخسران المفضي إلى الهلاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Tabbat may mean that Abu Lahab failed: he used his tribal authority to turn visitors away from the Prophet, but after the surah exposed his hostility, people distrusted him and his purpose failed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لأنه كان يدفع القوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The mention of his hand may recall how he put it on visitors’ shoulders to push them away while calling the Prophet mad.
rows.anchor: كان يضرب بيده على كتف الوافد عليه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A third interpretation says tabbat means Abu Lahab was overcome, since he imagined his hand would prevail by expelling and humiliating the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء تبت أي غلبت لأنه كان يعتقد أن يده هي العليا

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththab explains the phrase as his hands being empty of every good.
rows.anchor: صفرت يداه على كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hand may be singled out because Abu Lahab once took a stone intending to throw it at the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ما يرى أنه أخذ حجرا ليرمي به رسول الله

rows.speaker: طارق المحاربي
rows.claim: Tariq al-Muharibi reports seeing the Prophet preach in the market while a man stoned him and bloodied his heels; people identified the attacker as Abu Lahab, his uncle.
rows.anchor: طارق المحاربي أنه قال : رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hands can stand for the whole person or all one’s deeds, as in Qur’anic expressions about what hands have sent ahead and what they made.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { ذالك بما قدمت يداك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two hands may signify his religion and worldly life, his beginning and end, or his capacities to acquire benefit and ward off harm.
rows.anchor: تبت يداه أي دينه ودنياه أولاه وعقباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet visited Abu Lahab at night to invite him to Islam; a speaking goat kid praised the Prophet, and Abu Lahab tore apart its hands in envy, prompting the curse.
rows.anchor: جئتني معتذرا فجلس النبي عليه السلام أمامه

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports Abu Lahab mocked the Prophet’s promises of posthumous events as unreal, then blew on his hands and wished them ruin; the surah came down.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق : يروى أن أبا لهب كان يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first wording may be a curse against Abu Lahab, like the Qur’anic curse on the human being who refuses to believe.
rows.anchor: أخرج الأول مخرج الدعاء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both clauses may be factual reports: the first says his work perished and the second that he himself perished, leaving him without either kind of benefit.
rows.anchor: أراد بالأول هلاك عمله ، وبالثاني

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads the first clause as the loss of Abu Lahab’s wealth and the second as his own ruin.
rows.anchor: يعني ماله ومنه يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the hands Abu Lahab himself and reads the second clause as his son Utbah’s ruin after he rejected the Prophet and was killed by a lion in Syria.
rows.anchor: يعني نفسه : { وتب } يعني ولده عتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prediction can refer to Utbah’s later death because God already knew that it would occur.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان في معلومه تعالى أنه يحصل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses may also mean that Abu Lahab failed to recognize his Lord’s right and then failed to recognize the Messenger’s right.
rows.anchor: حيث لم يعرف حق ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use of Abu Lahab’s kunya is not necessarily honorific: kunyas can function as names, as illustrated by readings and names such as Ali ibn Abu Talib.
rows.anchor: أن التكنية قد تكون اسما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say the kunya became a proper name, replaced his birth name Abd al-Uzza, foretold his fiery end, or mocked his glowing cheeks.
rows.anchor: أنه كان اسمه عبد العزي فعدل عنه إلى كنيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s harsh address to his uncle is justified because Abu Lahab blocked the message by telling visitors Muhammad was mad; confronting him made his hostility public and his claims less credible.
rows.anchor: كان يصرف الناس عن محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Publicly confronting even his uncle showed that the Prophet would not compromise religious matters for anyone; if he would not spare his uncle, no one could expect favoritism.
rows.anchor: كان يداهن أحدا في الدين ويسامحه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship would ordinarily call for compassion, but Abu Lahab’s severe enmity reversed that expectation and made severe treatment fitting.
rows.anchor: حصلت العداوة العظيمة ، لا جرم استحق التغليظ العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike al-Kafirun, this surah does not command the Prophet to say the curse himself, sparing the respect due to his uncle’s kinship.
rows.anchor: رعاية الحرمة فلهذا السبب لم يقل له : قل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Kafirun the unbelievers attacked God, so God told Muhammad to answer; here they attacked Muhammad, so God answered them Himself.
rows.anchor: طعنوا في الله فقال الله تعالى : يا محمد أجب عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was to remain silent as the Qur’an instructs the servants of the Merciful to answer the ignorant peacefully, while God answered for him.
rows.anchor: فاسكت حتى تندرج تحت هذه الآية : { وإذا خاطبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says an angel defended Abu Bakr while he stayed silent, but withdrew when Abu Bakr began replying, when Satan came instead.
rows.anchor: حين كنت ساكتا كان الملك يجيب عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God defends, supports, and assists a person who does not directly answer a foolish or insulting speaker.
rows.anchor: من لا يشافه السفيه كان الله ذابا عنه وناصرا له ومعينا

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir of Mecca read Abu Lahab with a quiescent hā; Abu Ali explains Lahab and Lahb as dialect forms, though open hā is more eloquent in the other occurrences.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن كثير المكي حيث كان يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readers all open the hā in the later occurrences, which suggests the open form is preferable; another explanation is that their opening preserves the rhyme.
rows.anchor: إنما اتفقوا على الفتح في الثانية مراعاة لو فاق الفواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma aghna can be a rhetorical question asking what effect Abu Lahab’s wealth and gains could have had against disaster; even Qarun and Solomon could not avert death.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون استفهاما بمعنى الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wording is a direct statement that wealth and earnings did not help him.
rows.anchor: وعلى التقدير الثاني يكون ذلك إخبارا بأن المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ma kasaba is a raised relative or verbal noun, meaning either what he acquired or his earning.
rows.anchor: ما كسب مرفوع وما موصولة أو مصدرية يعني مكسوبه أو كسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab reportedly said that if his nephew’s message were true, he would ransom himself with his wealth and children; this verse answered him.
rows.anchor: إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا فأنا أفتدي منه نفسي بمالي وأولادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation distinguishes his capital from profits earned on it.
rows.anchor: لم ينفعه ماله وما كسب بماله يعني رأس المال والأرباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes his wealth as livestock and what he gained as their offspring and yield.
rows.anchor: المال هو الماشية وما كسب من نسلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view distinguishes inherited property from what Abu Lahab earned himself.
rows.anchor: الذي ورثه من أبيه والذي كسبه بنفسه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies what he gained with his children, supported by a hadith calling a man’s child part of his earnings; another report says Abu Lahab called his sons his wicked gains after they knocked him down.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { ما كسبت } ولده

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the phrase as Abu Lahab’s wealth and evil work, especially his plots against the Messenger.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك : ما ينفعه ماله وعمله الخبيث

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads it as deeds Abu Lahab thought would benefit him, like works rendered worthless in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : { وما كسب } أي عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the past tense is more emphatic than the future wording in al-Layl, as in other Qur’anic statements that use past verbs for certainty.
rows.anchor: التعبير بلفظ الماضي يكون آكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer is that wealth and earnings failed to let Abu Lahab defeat the Messenger in his hostility.
rows.anchor: في عداوة الرسول : فلم يغلب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that wealth and earnings could not save him from the Fire, as the next verse explains.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل لم يغنيا عنه في دفع النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from Abu Lahab’s past ruin and lack of benefit from wealth to his future entry into the Fire.
rows.anchor: لما أخبر تعالى عن حال أبي لهب في الماضي بالتباب وبأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb sayasla has readings with fatḥ or ḍamm on the yāʾ, in both light and doubled forms.
rows.anchor: قرىء بفتح الياء وبضمها مخففا ومشددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah predicted three unseen outcomes that came true: Abu Lahab’s ruin, wealth and children failing to help, and his dying an unbeliever destined for the Fire.
rows.anchor: الإخبار عنه بعدم الانتفاع بماله وولده

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi recounts that after Badr Abu Lahab learned that Muslims had lost but seen heavenly warriors; he struck Abu Rafi for identifying angels, was beaten by Umm al-Fadl, died of a disfiguring disease seven nights later, and his sons abandoned his body. This illustrates that wealth and family could not save him.
rows.anchor: روى أبو رافع مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Sunni theologians argue the surah entails an impossible obligation: Abu Lahab had to believe all divine reports, including God’s report that he would not believe, requiring belief in his own nonbelief.
rows.anchor: احتج أهل السنة على وقوع تكليف مالا يطاق بأن الله تعالى كلف أبا لهب بالإيمان

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbi and Abu al-Husayn al-Basri reply that had Abu Lahab believed, the report would have said he believed rather than that he did not.
rows.anchor: وأجاب الكعبي وأبو الحسين البصري بأنه لو آمن أبو لهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects that reply: the true divine report that Abu Lahab would not believe is inherently incompatible with actual belief, so commanding belief alongside it requires contradictory things.
rows.anchor: الخبر الصدق عن عدم إيمانه ينافيه وجود الإيمان منافاة ذاتية

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi answers that a hypothetical about God doing what He said He would not do cannot be answered with yes or no.
rows.anchor: لا يصح الجواب عن ذلك بلا أو نعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the Qadi’s answer also fails: reason recognizes the incompatibility between a true report of nonbelief and belief, whether an opponent answers aloud or stays silent.
rows.anchor: صريح العقل شاهد بأن بين كون الخبر عن عدم الإيمان صدقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for his wife has a diminutive reading; hammālata al-haṭab is also read accusative as an insult, a form al-Kashshaf prefers, with other accusative, indefinite, and nominative readings reported.
rows.anchor: قرىء ومريئنه بالتصغير وقرىء حمالة الحطب بالنصب على الشتم

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf prefers the accusative insult reading because it suits the Prophet’s loved ones’ dislike of Um Jamil.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف : وأنا أستحب هذه القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman is Um Jamil, daughter of Harb, sister of Abu Sufyan and aunt of Muawiya, and an extreme enemy of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أم جميل بنت حرب أخت أبي سفيان بن حرب عمة معاوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the phrase literally: she carried thorns at night and scattered them on the Prophet’s path; perhaps she was lowly despite wealth or acted herself from intense hatred.
rows.anchor: أنها كانت تحمل حزمة من الشوك والحسك فتنثرها بالليل في طريق رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view makes her a tale-bearer: carrying wood means stirring up conflict between people, and a night wood-gatherer is an idiom for someone collecting things blindly.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أنها كانت تمشي بالنميمة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says she taunted the Prophet for being poor, so she herself was described as gathering firewood.
rows.anchor: قول قتادة : أنها كانت تعير رسول الله بالفقر

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim and Saʿid ibn Jubayr read the wood as her sins in opposing the Prophet, which become a burden leading to Fire.
rows.anchor: قول أبي مسلم وسعيد بن جبير : أن المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the wife is nominative, she can be coordinated with the subject of will enter the Fire, with the neck-rope phrase circumstantial; alternatively she is a subject whose predicate is the phrase about her neck.
rows.anchor: امرأته إن رفعته ، ففيه وجهان أحدهما : العطف

rows.speaker: أسماء
rows.claim: Asma reports that Um Jamil arrived at the mosque shouting and carrying a stone after the surah came down; the Prophet said she could not see him and recited the verse about a hidden barrier.
rows.anchor: عن أسماء لما نزلت { تبت } جاءت أم جميل ولها ولولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashʿari theologians say sight is possible when its conditions exist but not necessary: God creates the perception if He wills, otherwise the person does not see.
rows.anchor: يكون الإدراك جائزا لا واجبا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Muʿtazilites explain that the Prophet may have turned away, while Um Jamil was too angry to inspect him, or that God placed fear in her heart.
rows.anchor: أعرض وجهه عنها وولاها ظهره

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Another Muʿtazilite explanation is that God made someone else appear in the Prophet’s place, as in the account of Jesus.
rows.anchor: ألقى شبه إنسان آخر على الرسول

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: A third explanation is that God redirected her eyesight away from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لعل الله تعالى حول شعاع بصرها عن ذلك السمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi objects that these proposals all show that a present thing may go unseen; if so, unseen elephants and unheard trumpets could also be present among us.
rows.anchor: أن يكون عندنا فيلات وبوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr’s denial that the Qur’an satirized Um Jamil is an equivocation: the Qur’an is not called satire, and its words are God’s, not the Prophet’s; the story supports the permissibility of equivocation.
rows.anchor: وهذا من باب المعاريض ، لأن القرآن لا يسمى هجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The epithet carrier of firewood specifies which wife was meant, since the Prophet supposedly had two other wives.
rows.anchor: كان له امرأتان سواها فأراد الله تعالى أن لا يظن ظان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning a woman is no objection when scripture also names the unbelieving wives of Noah and Lot; it is especially apt for the wife of an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: لما لم يستبعد في امرأة نوح وامرأة لوط بسبب كفر تينك المرأتين

none: section heading and verse heading only

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says masad means twisting: the term applies to well-twisted rope and to anything twisted, including camel hide, palm fiber, fronds, or iron.
rows.anchor: المسد في كلام العرب الفتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is a twisted cord around her neck to tie up the thorn bundle she carried, marking her lowly work and harming her and her husband.
rows.anchor: في جيدها حبل مما مسد من الحبال لأنها كانت تحمل تلك الحزمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation depicts her in Hell still carrying firewood from the Zaqqum tree with a rope of the Fire’s chains around her neck.
rows.anchor: أن حالها يكون في نار جهنم على الصورة التي كانت عليها حين كانت تحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cord can endure in Hell just as skin, flesh, and bone do; it may be made of iron, since masad means something twisted regardless of material.
rows.anchor: لأن المسد هو المفتول سواء كان من الحديد أو من غيره

none: bare chapter title and verse heading only

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: A report from Ubayy says reciting the chapter earns the reward of reciting a third of the Qur’an and ten good deeds for each person who believed or associated partners with God.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة قل هو الله أحد ، فكأنما قرأ

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another report says reciting the chapter once earns the reward of faith in God, His angels, books, and messengers, and the reward of one hundred martyrs.
rows.anchor: من قرأ قل هو الله أحد مرة واحدة أعطى من الأجر كمن آمن بالله

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Jibril says Abu Dharr is more famous among the angels than among people; his modest self-regard and frequent recitation of al-Ikhlas account for his distinction.
rows.anchor: فقال جبريل : هذا أبو ذر قد أقبل

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: At Tabuk, seventy thousand angels prayed for Muawiya ibn Muawiya; Jibril moved the mountains with his wing so the Prophet and companions could pray over him, and said his love of al-Ikhlas earned this honor.
rows.anchor: إن الله أمر أن ينزل من الملائكة سبعون ألف ملك فيصلوا على معاوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet heard a man invoke God as One and as-Samad and declare that He neither begets nor is born, and three times said the man was forgiven.
rows.anchor: غفر لك غفر لك غفر لك ثلاث مرات

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Saʿd reports that the Prophet told a poor man to greet his household or himself if alone and recite al-Ikhlas once; the man’s provision then expanded until he could supply his neighbors.
rows.anchor: إذا دخلت بيتك فسلم إن كان فيه أحد وإن لم يكن فيه أحد

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A man who recited al-Ikhlas in every prayer said he loved it, and the Prophet told him that this love would bring him into Paradise.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس : ( أن رجلا كان يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dream in which one recites it signifies tawhid, few dependents, much remembrance of God, and answered prayer.
rows.anchor: أعطي التوحيد وقلة العيال وكثرة الذكر لله

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that polytheists sent Amir ibn al-Tufayl to accuse Muhammad of division and insult, offering wealth, treatment, or marriage; they asked what material God was made of, and al-Ikhlas was revealed. Their objections prompted verses affirming God’s oneness and creation.
rows.anchor: إن المشركين أرسلوا عامر بن الطفيل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقالوا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports from Ibn Abbas that Jews with Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf asked who created God; Jibril calmed the angry Prophet, and al-Ikhlas was revealed. They then asked about God’s bodily form, and the verse declaring that they had not rightly measured God followed.
rows.anchor: روى عكرمة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata reports that Christians from Najran asked whether God was gemstone or metal; the Prophet said He is creator of things, not made of them. He explained that God’s oneness differs from human oneness, as-Samad is the one creation seeks, and the remaining clauses deny parentage and any peer.
rows.anchor: روى عطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chapter is called al-Tafrid, al-Tajrid, and al-Tawhid, names that emphasize singling God out and declaring His oneness.
rows.anchor: سورة التفريد وثانيها : سورة التجريد وثالثها : سورة التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called al-Ikhlas because it states only God’s negative attributes, makes its believer sincere, and promises rescue from Fire at death.
rows.anchor: سورة الإخلاص لأنه لم يذكر في هذه السورة سوى صفاته السلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its placement after the condemnation of Abu Lahab also inspires hope that its reciter will not be joined to him.
rows.anchor: ولأن ما قبله خلص في ذم أبي لهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the chapter of deliverance because it saves from anthropomorphism and disbelief in this world and from Hell in the next.
rows.anchor: سورة النجاة لأنها تنجيك عن التشبيه والكفر في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the chapter of friendship because reciters become God’s friends and knowing Him this way makes one His ally.
rows.anchor: سورة الولاية لأن من قرأها صار من أولياء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the chapter of lineage because it answered a request to describe God; a report tells a man of Sulaym to preserve God’s lineage, echoing Arab care for genealogies.
rows.anchor: سورة النسبة لما روينا أنه ورد جوابا لسؤال

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports that when a man recited al-Ikhlas, the Prophet said that this servant knew his Lord, so the chapter is called al-Maʿrifa.
rows.anchor: روى جابر أن رجلا صلى فقرأ

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: It is called al-Jamal in connection with the saying that God is beautiful and loves beauty; the chapter describes Him as One without equal, unlike a being who could have a counterpart.
rows.anchor: إن الله جميل يحب الجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muqashqisha means a healing cure: knowledge of the chapter cures shirk and hypocrisy, which the Qur’an calls a disease in hearts.
rows.anchor: لأن النفاق مرض كما قال : { فى قلوبهم مرض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chapter is called al-Muʿawwidhah because the Prophet used it with the two chapters after it for protection and said that no better protection had been sought.
rows.anchor: دخل على عثمان بن مظعون فعوذه بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called al-Samad because it is devoted to that divine attribute.
rows.anchor: سورة الصمد لأنها مختصة بذكره تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report calls it the foundation chapter and says the seven heavens and seven earths were founded on it.
rows.anchor: أسست السموات السبع والأرضون السبع على قل هو الله أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawhid supports the order of creation: belief in three gods threatens the heavens and earth, while a plurality of gods would cause both to collapse.
rows.anchor: لو كان فيهما الهة إلا الله لفسدتا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says God gave the Prophet al-Ikhlas from the treasures of His Throne during the ascension and named it al-Maniʿa because it prevents grave torment and fiery punishment.
rows.anchor: أعطيتك سورة الإخلاص وهي من ذخائر كنوز عرشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called al-Mahdar because angels attend to listen when it is recited.
rows.anchor: سورة المحضر لأن الملائكة تحضر لاستماعها إذا قرئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called al-Munaffira because Satan flees when it is recited.
rows.anchor: المنفرة لأن الشيطان ينفر عند قراءتها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: It is called al-Baraʾa because the Prophet said a reciter was free of shirk; another report promises freedom from Fire for reciting it one hundred times.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : من قرأ سورة قل هو الله أحد مائة مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called al-Mudhakkira because it recalls pure tawhid, like a mark that reminds the servant of what he neglects but needs.
rows.anchor: لأنها تذكر العبد خالص التوحيد فقراءة السورة كالوسمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called al-Nur because it illuminates the heart, as God is the light of the heavens and earth; the chapter is the Qur’an’s light and is to the Qur’an as the eye is to a person.
rows.anchor: إن لكل شيء نور ونور القرآن قل هو الله أحد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The name al-Aman comes from the report that whoever enters God’s fortress by declaring His oneness is safe from His punishment.
rows.anchor: إذا قال العبد لا إله إلا الله دخل حصني ومن دخل حصني أمن
